title: Introduction to CI/CD in Microsoft Fabric
summary: A vendor overview of Fabric's CI/CD platform, framing it as a layered stack: the Fabric REST API as the programmatic foundation, an integration/delivery layer (Git integration, deployment pipelines, Variable library), source-control automation in GitHub or Azure DevOps, and developer tooling (Fabric CLI, Terraform, fabric-cicd) for infrastructure as code.
audience: Platform engineers, DevOps leads, and Fabric admins designing a release process for Fabric workspaces and items.
why_it_matters: It gives architects the vocabulary and layering to reason about a Fabric CI/CD design end-to-end, and clarifies that every higher-level CI/CD experience (Git integration, deployment pipelines) is really just a client of the same underlying REST API surface — which matters when deciding whether to automate through the portal or through scripts/pipelines.
takeaways: All Fabric CI/CD capabilities are built on one common REST API foundation, so anything doable in the portal is also scriptable.
Git integration and deployment pipelines are complementary, not competing: Git handles day-to-day incremental development, pipelines handle staged promotion to test/prod.
The Variable library is Fabric's mechanism for configuration-as-code across pipeline stages.
A full enterprise setup pairs Fabric-side constructs (workspaces, capacities) with external CI infrastructure (GitHub/Azure DevOps runners, Key Vault, private networking).
Fabric CLI, Terraform, and the fabric-cicd Python library are the primary scripting/IaC tools, with fabric-cicd called out as the most widely adopted deployment tool.

claims.text: Every Fabric CI/CD capability, including Git integration and deployment pipelines, is built on top of the same underlying Fabric REST API surface for item CRUD, item definitions, capacity, workspace, access, and job operations.
Fabric Git integration lets a workspace sync with a repository in Azure DevOps or GitHub and supports service principal authentication for automated flows.

Deployment pipelines promote content across Dev, Test, and Prod stages using configuration rules and content comparison, and are intended to be paired with a Git-connected development workspace for the most efficient CI/CD workflow.

The Variable library provides configuration-as-code by letting teams define user-defined variables once, reference them across items such as lakehouse IDs or query definitions, and assign different values per deployment stage.

The Fabric CLI ('fab') is an open-source, scriptable command-line tool with a filesystem-like interface over Fabric, designed to run inside GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps pipelines for Git sync, deployment, and item management automation.

The Terraform provider for Microsoft Fabric provisions infrastructure such as workspaces and capacities, while the fabric-cicd Python library deploys item definitions from a source-controlled repository; fabric-cicd is described as the most widely adopted Fabric deployment tool.

In a reference enterprise CI/CD architecture, developer control tools sit above the Fabric REST API foundation, the integration/delivery layer runs the Variable library, Git integration, and deployment pipelines, and CI automation runs on a GitHub or Azure DevOps runner against Dev/Test/Prod Fabric capacities alongside supporting Azure resources like Key Vault and a private network.

Some Fabric item types supported by Git integration and deployment pipelines are still in preview, so item coverage should be checked against the current supported-items lists before relying on either feature for a given item type.
